contents.text:
I've settled that the core engine names no product: products are identities (who) and packs (what), plugged in at startup by a composition project. The reference is in src/docs/adr/0027-engine-identities-and-packs.md. I'll offer the user a few options on where to go next.

I'm weighing how to phrase the link to the doc path, keeping it short and putting the path last before the options.

ADR 0027 decides that the engine names no product. Puls, the coding agent and the other agents are built from two separate pieces that plug into it.

- **The engine (core)** holds the loop, sessions, usage and prices, guards, the contracts, and the tools every agent needs. It names no product and no country.
- **An identity** (`IAgentIdentity`) says who an agent is: its voice, modes, roles, and the packs it uses, by name.
- **A pack** (`IAgentPack`) says what an agent can do: toolsets, providers, guides and settings. A pack never references another pack or an identity.

A host picks identities and packs at start-up with `IDENTITIES` and `PACKS`. One composition project knows them all. The ADR gives the reason: Puls had grown inside core, so every product carried it.

Its consequences follow from that. A new product is configured rather than coded, and a new identity or pack adds no branch to core. Identities and packs load only at start-up, so a chat's tools never change while it runs.
